title: App guide
text: Using KetraTerm KetraTerm runs your local shells in tabs and split panes. Platform packages include a Java runtime; the Java-preinstalled archive requires Java 25. Shells and sessions Choose an installed shell from the profile menu when opening a terminal. Windows profiles include Windows PowerShell, PowerShell, Git Bash, WSL, Ubuntu, and Command Prompt. On macOS and Linux, KetraTerm discovers zsh, Bash, fish, Nushell, and sh. Profiles depend on the executables available on your machine; WSL discovery uses the default distribution. Use tabs for separate sessions and split panes to keep sessions side by side. Tabs can have custom names and accent colors. The app does not restore sessions after a restart. When a process exits unsuccessfully, the terminal retains its output and shows an exit-status banner with a Close button. Transport failures and exits without a reported status are retained too. You can still scroll, select, copy, and search; the ended session accepts no input. Closing it does not ask to kill a process. Successful exits keep the normal automatic close behavior. Commands and output Interactive PowerShell, Bash, zsh, and fish launches receive prompt hooks. These enable command markers, exit status, navigation between retained commands, and copying or exporting command output. WSL needs an explicitly selected supported shell for automatic hooks. Command Prompt and Nushell do not receive these hooks. Prompt customizations can affect command tracking. Use terminal search to find text in the visible screen and retained history. Copying reconstructs soft-wrapped lines. Hold Shift to use local mouse selection when a terminal application has enabled mouse reporting. Pasting text with line breaks or control characters opens a review dialog. Controls appear as escapes in a shortened preview. Choose Paste to submit the captured clipboard text, or Cancel to leave the running application untouched. Appearance and settings Open the settings dialog to choose a theme and font, adjust line height and cursor appearance, and configure shell and terminal permissions. Saved appearance settings update open panes. Process and buffer settings apply to new terminals. The settings reference lists configuration keys, defaults, and file locations. Restart the app after editing config.toml directly. Built-in keyboard shortcuts follow the platform. Keyboard, scrolling, and selection Action Windows Linux macOS Copy selection Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Shift+C Ctrl+Shift+C Cmd+C Paste Ctrl+V or Ctrl+Shift+V Ctrl+Shift+V Cmd+V New terminal Ctrl+Shift+T Ctrl+Shift+T Cmd+T Close active pane Ctrl+Shift+W Ctrl+Shift+W Cmd+W Search Ctrl+Shift+F Ctrl+Shift+F Cmd+Shift+F Increase / decrease font size Ctrl+Plus / Ctrl+Minus Ctrl+Plus / Ctrl+Minus Cmd+Plus / Cmd+Minus Reset font size Ctrl+0 Ctrl+0 Cmd+0 Next / previous tab Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+Shift+Tab Page through history Shift+Page Up / Shift+Page Down Shift+Page Up / Shift+Page Down Shift+Page Up / Shift+Page Down Oldest history / live output Shift+Home / Shift+End Shift+Home / Shift+End Shift+Home / Shift+End On Windows, Ctrl+C reaches the running program when nothing is selected. Font zoom affects only the current pane and is not saved. Reset restores the font size configured in settings. The equals key also increases the size with the platform modifier; numeric-keypad plus and minus work too. Wheel scrolling follows the operating system's scroll amount, and fractional trackpad motion accumulates without being discarded. Paging retains one row of context. New output follows the bottom while you are there and preserves your position when you scroll back; scroll_on_output can explicitly enable returning to the bottom on new output. Accepted terminal input or paste returns to live output. Terminal mouse reporting takes priority over local scrolling; alternate screen applications without mouse reporting can receive wheel motion as arrow keys. Drag to select text, double-click to select a word or path, and triple-click to select a row. Continuing a double- or triple-click drag extends by whole words or rows, including when you reverse direction. Alt+drag makes a rectangular selection. Copying preserves indentation and interior spaces, removes trailing row blanks, and joins soft wraps for a linear selection. Block selections keep their row breaks. Selection alone does not overwrite the clipboard. Hold Shift for local mouse interaction when an application reports mouse input, unless it explicitly requests Shift capture. Bare Ctrl+A and Ctrl+L remain available to the shell. Tab and pane shortcuts apply only in the app's own window. Companion commands Native local profiles include three helper commands: ketra version ketra info ketra config info reports the active configuration path; config opens that file using the helper's editor selection. WSL and Ubuntu launcher profiles do not receive the native helper. Completion KetraTerm suggestions are enabled by default. Use the Suggestions settings page to change inline previews, popup mode, shortcuts, and learning persistence. The master switch is also available in config.toml ; restart the app after editing the file directly: [behavior] smart_suggestions_enabled = true Suggestions need an editable command context from shell integration. Press Ctrl+Space to request them, use arrows or Page Up/Page Down to navigate, Tab to accept a deliberately selected item, and Escape to dismiss. Enter also accepts a deliberately selected suggestion by default. With no deliberate popup selection or visible inline text, Tab reaches the shell's own completion. When no editable shell context is available, Ctrl+Space reaches the running application instead. Suggestions combine built-in command specifications, local files and directories, and bounded learning. WSL or remote directory reports do not provide a remote filesystem completion service. Enable Inline suggestions on the Suggestions page to preview the first ranked completion as ghost text. This is off by default and works even when popups are disabled. Both surfaces use the same completion sources and ranking. If the top result would rewrite existing text, it remains popup-only; inline does not skip to another result. Right Arrow accepts a visible suffix while the popup is passive; Tab invokes shell completion. Up/Down select popup items and hide inline text; Tab or Enter then inserts that choice without execution. Fresh child suggestions remain passive for Tab and Enter: Tab invokes shell completion and Enter executes the directory already entered. Escape dismisses the popup first, then inline text. See the inline contract for matching and shell-prediction limits. Choose popup mode Off , On request , or Automatic . Automatic popups include command names by default; clear Include command names to show them only for parameters. Inline and popup presentation can be enabled independently; the master switch disables both. The three shortcut rows control accepting inline text, accepting a selected popup item, and opening the popup. Click + , then press the shortcut to add it. Click a chip to remove it; removing every chip disables that action. Remove Enter from Accept selected popup to keep Enter available to the shell. Learning stays in memory unless persistence is enabled explicitly. Persisted learning can include plaintext command data; filtering cannot identify every secret. Treat the learning file as sensitive. See the persistence setting in the settings reference . Terminal permissions Clipboard permissions control requests from programs running in a terminal, including nested SSH sessions. They are separate from your explicit copy and paste actions. New configurations allow clipboard writes and ask before reads; you can change this in settings. Window manipulation is disabled by default. Invalid explicit clipboard or title permissions deny access and report the affected key and configuration file. If the whole file cannot be loaded, these permissions are denied in the recovery configuration as well. See the app changelog for changes by release.

title: Settings reference
text: App settings The standalone application stores one preferences snapshot in config.toml . Use the settings dialog for live updates. Direct file edits take effect on the next application launch. This file belongs to the standalone product; embedded libraries and the IntelliJ plugin have their own configuration owners. 1. TOML Configuration Syntax The application accepts section headers, one key = value per physical line, booleans, numbers, quoted strings, and comments. Use the generated file as the format template: the parser implements this configuration subset, rather than the full TOML language. Arrays, inline tables, and multiline values are not configuration values. Double-quoted strings (including triple-quoted strings on one line) decode TOML 1.0 escapes: \b , \t , \n , \f , \r , \" , \\ , \uXXXX , and \UXXXXXXXX . Unicode escapes must identify scalar values. Single-quoted strings preserve backslashes literally. Malformed strings, unsupported escapes, and text after a closing delimiter other than a # comment are rejected. A small configuration can override only the preferences you need: [window] columns = 120 rows = 35 scrollback_lines = 5000 [font] size = 16 line_height = 1.0 [theme] name = "nord" [shell] path = "bash" startup_command = "" [security] clipboard_write = "allow" clipboard_read = "prompt" title_permission = "allow" Window, font, and theme Section Key Default Accepted values window columns 100 Integer, 10..1000. window rows 28 Integer, 10..500. window scrollback_lines 10000 Integer, 0..1000000. font family Platform default Installed family name. Windows: Cascadia Mono ; macOS: Menlo ; elsewhere: the first installed family in Swing's curated monospace list, falling back to Monospaced . font size 16 Integer points, 10..56. font line_height 1.0 Multiplier, 0.7..1.5. font use_system_fallback_fonts true Boolean; permits installed system fonts as fallback. theme name one-dark campbell , one-dark , nord , tokyo-night , everforest . Unknown theme identifiers use one-dark at rendering time. Font selection uses Swing's font-family resolution and fallback rules. Window and scrollback values are initial settings for new terminals, rather than requests to replace an existing process or history buffer. The initial window is centered within its monitor's usable area, excluding taskbars and docks. Oversized windows shrink to fit; the session receives the resulting visible grid before shell output starts. The saved dimensions are not rewritten. Defaults apply to new configuration files and omitted preferences. Explicitly saved window dimensions, scrollback capacity, fonts, and cursor preferences are preserved when the application is upgraded. Behavior All keys below belong to [behavior] . Boolean values are true or false . Key Default Meaning or accepted values cursor_shape "block" block , underline , or beam ; unknown values render as a block. cursor_blink_millis 600 Integer, 0..10000; zero disables blinking. prompt_decoration "gutter" gutter , divider , or none , ignoring case. treat_ambiguous_as_wide false East Asian Ambiguous characters occupy two cells. audible_bell true System beep on BEL. visual_bell true Visual pulse on BEL. paste_on_middle_click true Middle-button gesture pastes ordinary clipboard text. paste_sanitization "preserve" preserve or strip-c0 ; bracketed-paste framing is protected in both. shell_request_resize_window false Permit terminal-originated grid-size requests to resize the window. shell_request_window_manipulation false Permit terminal-originated move, minimize, maximize, raise, and lower requests. desktop_notifications_enabled true Master permission for OSC 9/777 notifications and command-finished alerts. command_finished_alerts_enabled false Notify when a long-running command finishes while its originating pane is unfocused; requires shell integration. command_finished_alert_threshold_seconds 10 Inclusive minimum observed command duration; clamped to 1..86400 seconds. smart_suggestions_enabled true Master switch for completion and learning. shell_suggestions_enabled true Automatic popups for eligible shell profiles, including PowerShell; requires the master and popup switches. Explicit requests do not require this automatic-popup switch. popup_suggestions_enabled true Enable the popup surface, including explicit requests; independent of inline previews. popup_accept_keys "TAB" Insert a deliberately selected popup item; passive popups leave the key to inline suggestions or the shell. popup_selected_accept_keys "ENTER" Insert only a deliberately selected popup item, without execution. inline_accept_keys "RIGHT" Insert the whole visible inline suggestion while the popup is passive. suggestions_trigger_keys "ctrl SPACE" Explicitly open the popup and select its first available item. inline_suggestions_enabled false Preview the top ranked completion as an append-only inline suffix, when the master switch is enabled. Independent of popup presentation; see inline previews . shell_suggestion_automatic_mode "always" "always" or "parameters_only" . The latter suppresses executable-name popups; subcommands, options, arguments, and explicit completion remain available. accept_selected_suggestion_with_enter true Enter inserts a deliberately selected suggestion without execution; automatic highlighting and hover remain shell-owned. Disable to keep Enter shell-owned. suggestion_learning_persistence_enabled false Persist compact completion-learning metadata when completion is enabled. sticky_command_headers_enabled true Repeat the full original prompt/input row above scrolled command output, with unchanged terminal typography. scroll_on_output false Return to live output when new rows enter history. Typing and accepted paste always reveal live input. show_foreground_process_name true Use a detected process name when it does not supply a title; custom names retain priority. Command-finished alerts use monotonic time between shell markers and recheck the originating pane's keyboard focus, current preferences, and lifetime before display. Pending completions coalesce to one alert per session while the UI is busy; command text is never included in these alerts. Suggestion bindings are comma-separated pressed Swing key strokes, such as TAB , RIGHT , ctrl SPACE , or shift TAB . A blank string disables the action. Malformed file values fall back per field. Saved values may include the explicit pressed token, for example ctrl pressed SPACE . Strings are confined to TOML; the app uses typed KeyStroke values internally. The Suggestions settings page records key presses and displays removable chips instead of editable strings. The two popup acceptance fields form one Accept selected popup row. Removing Enter there also disables accept_selected_suggestion_with_enter . Popup navigation and dismissal retain their standard keys. Library consumers can replace the complete keymaps through the public Swing API. The former inline_history_suggestions_enabled key is read when inline_suggestions_enabled is absent. Saving writes the current key and preserves the saved on/off choice. Use the master switch to disable all suggestions. To use only inline previews, enable it and disable popup_suggestions_enabled ; to use only popups, leave inline previews off. shell_suggestions_enabled = false keeps explicit popups available when the popup surface is enabled. These combinations appear in the settings page as popup modes Off , On request , and Automatic . Paste handling is independent of the local PTY's newline policy. Legacy raw and normalize-line-endings values load as preserve ; saving writes the canonical value. See the paste contract for control-character and framing rules. Explicit clipboard and middle-button pastes containing line breaks or control characters other than Tab require confirmation. The preview is limited to 400 Unicode codepoints and shows controls as escapes; Cancel is selected initially. Approval submits the original captured text through the configured paste policy. This review also applies when bracketed paste is active. Safe single-line text does not prompt. Terminal-originated clipboard requests use their separate permissions. Bell bursts coalesce into one pending UI task per window, retaining at most 64 originating panes. Feedback is limited to one delivery every 500 ms per window; one delivery can flash multiple panes but sounds only once. Closing the window cancels queued bells, and feedback rechecks current settings and pane lifetime. Persisted completion data is stored beside the configuration file. See the storage reference for retained ranking data, command replay, and privacy limits. Shell launch and startup command [shell] key Default Meaning path Platform shell One executable path or command name. Windows: discovered pwsh.exe , falling back to powershell.exe ; elsewhere: $SHELL , falling back to /bin/bash . A blank value uses this default. start_directory User home Working directory for new terminals. startup_command "" One shell command line to submit after the first complete interactive prompt; blank disables it. path is not a shell command line containing arguments. Use application launch arguments for a one-off process command. Discovered profiles may supply their normal shell flags when the executable matches a known profile. For example, startup_command = 'npm run dev' runs once in each new terminal. It requires a directly configured interactive PowerShell, Bash, zsh, or fish shell with startup hooks enabled. WSL launchers, unsupported shells, and explicit command/script entry points cannot use it; incompatible launches report an error. User input before submission cancels the pending command. Commands are interpreted by the selected shell, with no additional host quoting or expansion. Use a script for multiline programs. The limit is 16384 UTF-16 code units, with no control characters. For Windows paths, single-quoted literal strings preserve backslashes: path = 'C:\tools\pwsh.exe' . Keep each value on one physical line. The settings writer preserves quotes, significant whitespace, Unicode, and backslashes using single-line triple-quoted strings. Saving replaces the file with canonical generated content, so custom comments and unknown keys are not retained. Terminal-originated permissions All keys below belong to [security] . Permissions cover the whole terminal session, including nested SSH and multiplexer output. Key New-file default Accepted values clipboard_write "allow" allow , prompt , deny . clipboard_read "prompt" allow , prompt , deny . Existing files with a missing or invalid value use deny . clipboard_max_decoded_bytes 1048576 Integer, 0..2147483647; decoded UTF-8 limit for clipboard reads and writes. title_permission "allow" allow , deny . The settings dialog labels prompt as Ask. These permissions govern terminal requests, rather than the user's explicit copy or paste actions. Removed local/remote permission keys are ignored; use the session-wide keys above. Explicit invalid or empty clipboard_write , clipboard_read , and title_permission values use deny and report the affected key and file path on standard error, without echoing the invalid value. Other valid preferences remain effective. Omitted write/title fields use their defaults; omitted read permissions in existing files remain denied. 2. Directory Resolution Hierarchy The first nonblank override wins: JVM system property ketraterm.config.path . Environment variable KetraTerm_CONFIG_PATH . Platform default shown below. Platform Configuration file Windows %APPDATA%\KetraTerm\config.toml ; without APPDATA , ~\.config\ketraterm\config.toml . macOS ~/Library/Application Support/KetraTerm/config.toml . Linux and other platforms $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ketraterm/config.toml ; without a valid absolute XDG_CONFIG_HOME , ~/.config/ketraterm/config.toml . Override values name the file, rather than its parent directory. The app's ketra info companion command reports the active path; ketra config opens it through the helper's editor selection. Native helpers are not installed into WSL or Ubuntu launcher profiles. Default installations keep learned suggestions in the platform's persistent-state location; nondefault configuration paths retain colocated learning. See storage locations and migration . 3. Configuration Backup & Fallback Lifecycle A missing file is generated with defaults, including clipboard reads set to prompt . If generation fails, the app reports the write failure and uses the defaults in memory. Numeric values outside their bounds are clamped, including integer overflow. Malformed numbers and invalid booleans use the corresponding field default. Existing files use deny for missing or invalid clipboard-read permissions. A parse or configuration-validation failure moves the existing file to <filename>.broken , replacing any previous backup, then attempts to write a default file. These recovery defaults deny clipboard reads, clipboard writes, and title changes. A failed backup leaves the original file in place and returns the recovery defaults. An I/O read failure is reported and uses recovery defaults without backing up or replacing the unreadable file. Settings saves stage a complete snapshot beside the destination and require atomic replacement. A failed save preserves the previous file and active settings. Successful saves publish the snapshot to consumers on the EDT. See README.md for application launch and Module.md for application structure and dependencies.

title: App changelog
text: KetraTerm Standalone Changelog Release notes for the KetraTerm desktop application. For emulator APIs and embedding changes, see the library changelog . Released versions: 1.0.1 · 1.0.0 · 0.5.0 · 0.4.0 · 0.3.0 · 0.2.2 · 0.2.1 · 0.2.0 · 0.1.3 · 0.1.2 · 0.1.1 · 0.1.0 [1.0.1] - 2026-11-18 Improvements Double-click to select a whole word or path across visible wrapped rows, including URL fragments such as #install . Completion popups show the text that will be inserted, including path prefixes and quotes. Up dismisses automatic suggestions and recalls command history. Further Up/Down presses stay with the shell until typing resumes or completion is requested. Fixed Preserve REPLY between commands in Bash and zsh, and keep zsh directory reports accurate with Korn-style array indexing enabled. Keep shell integration working when reloading a zsh or fish prompt theme. Keep custom PowerShell F12 shortcuts when opening a terminal or rebinding keys. Keep custom PowerShell prompt indicators accurate after a command fails. Complete Windows paths such as /logs/ on the terminal's current drive. Resolve PowerShell completion and relative file links from the correct directory when using a session drive or a folder name containing a literal percent escape. Show the final success or failure of PowerShell lines that mix native commands and cmdlets, and retain exact native failure codes when they repeat. Keep Bash startup DEBUG hooks working across prompts while preserving directory updates and suggestions. Keep split panes aligned in full-screen applications that display bidirectional text. The cursor returns to its correct position when widening the window after narrowing moves only the cursor onto the next line. Exiting a resized full-screen application no longer overwrites earlier output. Sticky command headers remain visible while typing refreshes the prompt layout. [1.0.0] - 2026-11-17 Suggestions Added optional inline suggestions, accepted with Right Arrow, even with popups disabled. Suggestion popups show alternatives to the inline preview. After browsing, Tab or Enter inserts the selected suggestion without running it. Added a Suggestions settings page for inline previews, popups, saved learning, and shortcuts. Improved PowerShell suggestions when native predictions are visible. Ctrl+Space reaches the running application when shell suggestions are unavailable. Saved suggestions move automatically to standard per-user storage for default configurations. Keyboard, selection, and navigation Improved responsiveness when copying large selections, exporting output, pasting, and opening links. Added temporary font zoom and reset per pane, plus Ctrl+Shift+C/V for copy and paste on Windows. Tab and pane shortcuts apply to the active window. History paging keeps one row of context; Shift+Home/End jumps to the oldest history or live output. Double- and triple-click dragging selects whole words or rows, with improved word selection. Startup and session recovery Improved startup and responsiveness when opening tabs, splits, settings, and directory menus. Fixed quoted text and Windows paths in manually edited configuration files. New configurations use 100 × 28 cells and 10,000 scrollback lines; the initial window fits the desktop. Improved default monospace font selection on Linux and other non-Windows/macOS platforms. Linux installers preserve the KetraTerm icon and associate running windows with the application launcher. macOS disk images use the KetraTerm volume icon. New Windows configurations prefer modern PowerShell when installed, preserving saved shell choices. Failed sessions keep their output with an exit-status banner and Close button. Security and notifications Protected the bundled ketra command against tampering. Multiline pastes and pastes with control characters show a review dialog with Cancel selected. Invalid clipboard or title permissions block access and identify the affected setting. Limited repeated bell alerts to twice per second per window. [0.5.0] - 2026-11-09 Suggestions Expanded experimental suggestions with PowerShell completions, Bash/zsh command discovery, command specifications, local paths, and Git references. Suggestions are enabled by default; saved learning is opt-in. See shell requirements . Added match highlighting, argument hints, and settings for automatic popups and Enter acceptance. PowerShell prediction redraws preserve suggestions; changed input invalidates acceptance. Appearance and navigation Improved shell icon contrast and proportions, including a clearer Command Prompt icon. Added sticky command headers, enabled by default. Click a header to return to its command; disable the overlay independently in settings. Typing and pasting return immediately to live input. Scroll on output now defaults to off; saved preferences remain effective. [0.4.0] - 2026-10-31 Terminal features Compatible applications can show progress rings in shell icons and window/taskbar status where supported. Progress works independently of titles and clears after five minutes without updates. Added Kitty image previews for RGB/RGBA and PNG, including compression, cropping, and scaling. Compatible applications can change the mouse pointer shape. Search Added whole-word and regular-expression search, with feedback for invalid patterns. Search stays responsive in large histories, updates results during scanning, and starts at the viewport. Queries with many matches show 1,000+ ; navigation still reaches all retained matches. Search controls fit narrow panes, follow the theme, and show shortcut hints and keyboard focus. Alt+C/W/R toggles case, whole words, and regex; Enter/Shift+Enter navigates; Escape closes search. Fixed highlight remnants after changing a selected match to a query with no results. Appearance and layout Added Gutter, Divider, and None prompt styles. Integrated shells reserve their gutter at startup. Centered full-screen terminal applications consistently across shell profiles. Unfocused terminals keep visible cursors: outlined blocks or steady bars and underlines. Improved link highlighting across wrapped lines, scrolling, and output updates. Fixed layout errors after prompt-style changes, window moves, and resizing near desktop edges. Suggestions and notifications Stale suggestions no longer affect newer input. Closing a terminal or disabling suggestions closes its popup. Added opt-in alerts for long-running commands that finish in an unfocused terminal, with a configurable duration threshold of 10 seconds by default. Security and permissions Compatible applications can read clipboard text with consent. Dialogs offer one-time approval, denial, or blocking for the terminal; new settings ask before reading. Clipboard and title permissions now apply throughout a session, including SSH. Clipboard choices are Deny, Ask, and Allow; writes default to Allow. Previous local/remote settings reset to defaults. Improved paste protection and simplified paste settings. Unsupported status queries can no longer inject supplied text or control characters into input. Compatibility and reliability Improved cursor-position, cursor-style, modifier-key, and terminal-capability query compatibility. Fixed column switching when window resizing is disabled or the layout cannot resize. Improved large-paste reliability and prevented premature writes during terminal startup. Input settings can change safely during a paste. Improved combined text formatting and rejected oversized commands safely. Improved responsiveness during large output and window-state reporting while output is active. [0.3.0] - 2026-09-23 Shells and startup Tabs can show the running application's name when no title is supplied. Custom names take priority, and automatic process titles can be disabled. Added startup commands for new tabs and splits, with improved custom shell startup compatibility. Scrolling, selection, and links Fixed scrolling in split layouts disturbing neighboring content and slow trackpad gestures being ignored in full-screen applications when mouse mode is off. Fixed cursor and scroll-position jumps when resizing with a full history. Fixed missing spaces and line breaks when copying or exporting text after resizing. Fixed links opening the wrong destination after reset and improved wrapped-link highlighting. Compatible applications can copy up to 1 MiB to the clipboard, subject to permissions. Terminal compatibility Fixed cursor shape and blinking after leaving full-screen applications such as Neovim. Improved cursor save/restore and terminal-width switching while respecting resize settings and protecting split layouts. Compatible applications can detect the terminal's light or dark theme. [0.2.2] - 2026-09-11 Unicode and text rendering Aligned Hebrew, Arabic, and mixed-direction text with backgrounds, cursors, selections, search highlights, and mouse targets. Fixed Arabic shaping under block cursors, missing text in long shaped lines, and unexpected font changes around joiners, particularly on macOS. Preserved native emoji and solid block graphics on lines containing right-to-left text. Selection and display fixes Concealed text stays hidden under cursors and link highlights; neighboring glyphs stay clipped. Fixed rectangular selections widening across mixed-direction or partially hidden rows. Switching sessions clears the previous session's text and search results. Fixed blinking text, cursor visibility, and reverse-video updates in scrollback. Fixed smooth-scroll gaps and jumps during loading, resizing, and screen switches. [0.2.1] - 2026-07-14 Input and compatibility Fixed held Backspace and Delete keys deleting only one character. Improved Ctrl-number shortcuts, modified keys, extended function keys, and Backspace behavior. Improved capability reporting and compatibility with applications that verify screen regions. [0.2.0] - 2026-07-13 Clipboard and selection Fixed multiline paste and intermittent copies of incorrect or stale text. Improved copying of scrollback selections, wrapped lines, and trailing empty cells. Fixed prompt gutter clicks selecting the wrong text. Scrolling Restored historical output scrolling in terminal applications using scroll regions. [0.1.3] - 2026-07-08 Search and shortcuts Added a floating search bar with result navigation and case-sensitive matching. Improved copy, paste, search, and scrolling shortcuts, including standard macOS Cmd bindings. Added a context menu that respects terminal mouse tracking. [0.1.2] - 2026-07-03 Settings and fixes Added process close confirmation and a Scroll on output setting. Fixed copying selections across the entire scrollback history and first-run TUI wrapping. [0.1.1] - 2026-07-02 Input fixes Fixed AltGr input and grid corruption on AZERTY keyboards for Windows/Linux. [0.1.0] - 2026-06-30 Initial release First public standalone desktop release, with tabs, custom titles, and tab shortcuts. Added local sessions for zsh, bash, sh, PowerShell, and cmd.exe. Added configurable typography, colors, palettes, and scrollback capacity.
